# ANVIL rules: typescript

Follow these rules for typescript code (**/*.ts, **/*.js, **/*.mjs, **/*.tsx).

## Node.js

# Node.js
- Use `node:` prefixed built-ins; `fs/promises` over sync I/O on hot paths.
- Spawn processes with argument arrays (`execFile`/`spawn`), never shell strings with user input.
- Validate environment variables at startup; fail fast with clear messages.
- Handle `unhandledRejection` and stream errors.

## TypeScript

# TypeScript

- `strict` mode; no `any` without a comment explaining why. Use `unknown` and narrow.
- Validate external data at boundaries (schema validation) before trusting its type.
- Await every promise or handle it explicitly; no floating promises.
- Prefer `const`, readonly types and discriminated unions for state.
- Use `node:` prefixed built-ins in Node code.

## TypeScript Testing

# TypeScript Testing

- Use the project's runner (Vitest/Jest). Co-locate or mirror source layout consistently.
- Use fake timers and dependency injection instead of sleeps and real network.
- Type-check tests too.
